note: CKEditor5 Bootstrap Tabs ships a CKEditor 5 plugin (ckeditor5-bootstrap-tabs.BootstrapTabs) that registers the 'bootstrapTabs' toolbar item for inserting Bootstrap tab markup. Depends on ckeditor5. It has no configure route, no settings form, no config entity of its own, no permissions, no Drush - you enable it by adding 'bootstrapTabs' to a text format's CKEditor 5 toolbar, stored in editor.editor.<format> settings.toolbar.items. Medium/hard cases use namespaced ckbt_* text formats + editors and are verified against the editor config entity's toolbar items. All fixtures are removed on cleanup; no shared/real text format is touched.

evals.prompt: How do I let editors insert Bootstrap tabs using the ckeditor_bootstrap_tabs module - i.e. how do I turn it on for a text format?
evals.expected_output: Edit a CKEditor 5 text format at Configuration > Content authoring > Text formats and editors, and drag the 'Bootstrap Tabs' button into the active toolbar (adds the 'bootstrapTabs' item to editor.editor.<format> settings.toolbar.items). Ensure the format's allowed HTML permits the tab markup.

evals.prompt: What does the ckeditor_bootstrap_tabs module depend on, and what kind of markup does its widget produce?
evals.expected_output: It depends on the ckeditor5 module. Its widget outputs Bootstrap tab markup: a ul.nav.nav-tabs list of tab-link triggers plus a div.tab-content with div.tab-pane panels (the elements it declares as allowed).

evals.prompt: In the ckeditor_bootstrap_tabs module, what is the machine name of the CKEditor 5 toolbar item (button) that inserts a tabs widget, and where in configuration is it recorded when enabled?
evals.expected_output: The toolbar item is 'bootstrapTabs' (CKEditor 5 plugin ckeditor5-bootstrap-tabs.BootstrapTabs). When enabled it is listed in editor.editor.<format> under settings.toolbar.items.

evals.prompt: This Drupal site has a text format 'ckbt_probe' using CKEditor 5. Inspect the live editor configuration and tell me whether the Bootstrap Tabs button is enabled on it (and name the toolbar item).
evals.expected_output: Yes - editor.editor.ckbt_probe has 'bootstrapTabs' in settings.toolbar.items, so the Bootstrap Tabs button is enabled. Check with `drush cget editor.editor.ckbt_probe settings.toolbar.items`.

evals.prompt: This site has two CKEditor 5 text formats, ckbt_on and ckbt_off. Exactly one of them has the Bootstrap Tabs button in its toolbar. Inspect the live configuration and state which format has it enabled.
evals.expected_output: ckbt_on has 'bootstrapTabs' in its editor toolbar items; ckbt_off does not.

evals.prompt: On this Drupal site there is a CKEditor 5 text format 'ckbt_task' whose toolbar does not yet include the Bootstrap Tabs button. Using the ckeditor_bootstrap_tabs module, add the Bootstrap Tabs button to that format's CKEditor 5 toolbar. Apply the change to the live site.
evals.expected_output: Add 'bootstrapTabs' to editor.editor.ckbt_task settings.toolbar.items (via the Text format's toolbar drag-and-drop, or by editing the editor config).

evals.prompt: The rich-text editor for the 'ckbt_task2' text format on this site is missing the tool that lets editors insert Bootstrap tabs. Enable that tool for this format so editors can add tabbed content. Apply the change to the live site.
evals.expected_output: Add the 'bootstrapTabs' toolbar item to editor.editor.ckbt_task2 settings.toolbar.items (the Bootstrap Tabs button from the ckeditor_bootstrap_tabs module).
